newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican truck drivers threaten freeway protest.
newsitem.headline: Mexican truck drivers threaten freeway protest.

text.p: Some 40,000 independent Mexican truckers threatened Monday to protest on the country's main freeways, without blocking traffic, if the government continues to refuse to negotiate the truckers' demands.

Truckers said the government had refused to discuss the drivers' demands of lower diesel prices, more protection from crooked policeman and highway assaults and less red tape for licenses and permits.

"As the (government) is denying there is a work stoppage, we are going out to the freeways tomorrow if necessary, without blocking the freeways, so they can see that we are on strike," the National Confederation of Commercial Truckers Edmundo Delgado told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Most cargo in Mexico is carried by truck. The Communications and Transport Ministry said in a statement that the announced work stoppage "does not have the support of truck drivers...and all activity in the sector is carrying on totally as normal."
But if the strike lasts more than a day or two, farmers predicted a delay in shipments and scheduled deliveries.
Coffee farmer Ernesto Gutierrez said he would not be able to meet strict delivery schedules.
"There is no transportation," he told Reuters. "We do not dare to use our own trucks because the truckers could get violent and our insurance would not cover it," he said.

The director general of Mexico City's produce supply center, Rafael Munoz Praga, said despite the strike, the city has sufficient supply in reserves to last six days, with each day's supply about 27,000 tonnes of produce.
Delgado's independent truckers association, which represents between 10 and 15 percent of the nation's truck drivers, began a nationwide strike Monday at dawn.

The confederation is asking for a 40 percent reduction of diesel prices, currently about 2.28 pesos per liter. Delgado said the drivers also want more security measures, not just from highway bandits but from corrupt policemen.
Delgado also charged the federal police with threatening to plant drugs to extort truck drivers. An average 30 trucks per day are victims of theft, he added.
